_comment: Single source of truth for PatchStorage listing metadata. One entry per plugin short-name (matches the LV2 URI suffix and the <name>.lv2 bundle). generate_metadata.py renders this into the uploader's plugins.json (source/donate/license/categories/tags) plus a LISTINGS.md per target; split_bundle.py injects 'long' into each bundle TTL as rdfs:comment, which is what PatchStorage shows as the listing description. Source/donate links live ONLY in the structured source_code_url/donate_url fields (which become the profile/listing buttons) — NOT repeated in the description body. 'nam' marks the NAM-capable plugins: NAM is present on linux-amd64 + rpi-aarch64 and hidden on patchbox-os-arm32. STYLE RULE: no trademarked device/brand/artist names anywhere in titles, shorts, longs or tags — describe circuits by type and use the suite's own parody names (word play) for devices.

amp.title: Hex Chain Amp
amp.short: Eleven original guitar-amp voicings — sparkling clean to modern high-gain — each with a modeled power amp, plus a NAM loader.
amp.long:
A whole wall of amps in one plugin — ELEVEN original voicings, every name a wink and every circuit tuned against real-amp captures:

- Clean Meanie — shimmering American blackface-era clean
- Crunchy McCrunchFace — hot-rodded British master-volume crunch
- Gainzilla — tight modern high-gain monster
- Doom Daddy — a doom/fuzz grinder with two full channels (Normal + Brite)
- Tangerang — thick, mid-forward British lead crunch
- Beardo BE — boutique hot-rod head with Clean / BE / HBE channels
- Hi-Volt — high-headroom, pedal-loving British clean
- Chime Thirty — chimey class-A jangle machine
- Backline Plus — the scrappy solid-state combo every rehearsal room owns
- Plexiglass — vintage British sparkle with jumpered Vol I + Vol II channels, just like bridging the inputs on the classic four-hole heads
- Cali V — a 9-mode, three-channel Californian switcher (Clean / Crunch / Lead) with its own 5-band graphic EQ

Every voicing feeds a modeled power-amp section — sag, presence, depth, resonance and selectable output-tube flavors — for real cab-pushing feel and touch dynamics rather than a flat distortion. A shared tone stack keeps switching between voicings fast on stage, a built-in mains-hum filter and decay-aware noise conditioning keep the high-gain modes quiet between notes, and everything is oversampled with steep anti-alias filtering so the top end stays clean.

On 64-bit/desktop targets a Neural (NAM) slot loads your own .nam amp captures alongside the eleven algorithmic models; on 32-bit (patchbox-os-arm32) NAM is omitted. Works standalone or as part of the Hex Chain suite / Hex Forge.

Free and open source (GPL-3). All device names are original parodies; tonal descriptions reference amp types and circuits, not brands — all trademarks are the property of their respective owners, and no affiliation or endorsement is implied.

Credit: Ryan Powell

cab.title: Hex Chain Cab
cab.short: Cabinet sim: six built-in cabs + your own .wav IRs, a draggable mic-placement pad, and adjustable room ambience.
cab.long:
A convolution cabinet with a studio's worth of mic technique built in.

SIX built-in cabs cover the classics without shipping a single sampled IR: the Factory 4x12 (Thirty-Something ceramic bite), Chime 2x12 (alnico sparkle), American 2x12 (open-back spread), Cashback 4x12 (woody vintage crunch), Hi-Volt 4x12 (big, fast and clean) and Doom 4x12 (huge + dark). Each one is synthesized with measured-IR anatomy — cone-breakup ripple, baffle reflections and box resonance — so they fingerprint like real cabs, and they're loudness-matched so switching never jumps in volume.

MIC PLACEMENT is a draggable pad, not a knob bank: slide the mic from the cap to the cone edge and pull it back up to ~30 cm — position darkens and thickens like moving off-axis, distance trades proximity punch for room air. It works on the built-in cabs AND your own IRs, and it saves with presets.

ROOM ambience adds a compact stereo small-to-medium room behind the cab (toggle, mix and size), so direct rigs stop sounding like a speaker pressed against your eardrum. Also preset-savable.

Load your own .wav impulse responses through the file browser — they're resampled with windowed-sinc quality, so a 44.1 kHz IR keeps its top end intact. Low-cut, high-cut and dry/wet mix finish the voicing.

Ships making sound out of the box. Free and open source (GPL-3). Cab names are original word play; no affiliation with any speaker or cabinet manufacturer is implied.

drive.title: Hex Chain Drive
drive.short: Seven original overdrive, boost & distortion voicings + a NAM loader.
drive.long:
Seven original drive, boost and distortion voicings in one pedal, each with drive, tone, level and dry/wet mix:

- Green Man — the mid-humped green legend that pushes an amp into song
- New Dawn — smooth, singing overdrive for lead work
- Dear Rodent Boy — snarling rodent-toothed distortion
- Grunge DS — the bright orange distortion box that soundtracked the flannel decade
- Gilded Horse — the mythical gold transparent overdrive/boost (yes, that one)
- Super Nova — a smooth super-overdrive with a warm asymmetric clip
- Preamp 250 — gritty '70s preamp-in-a-box distortion

Stack them in front of the Hex Chain Amp or your own rig. On 64-bit/desktop targets a Neural (NAM) slot runs your own .nam pedal captures alongside the seven algorithmic voicings; on 32-bit (patchbox-os-arm32) NAM is omitted.

Free and open source (GPL-3). Names are original parodies and are not affiliated with any manufacturer.

fuzz.title: Hex Chain Fuzz
fuzz.short: Four fuzz pedals in one: multi-era sustain machine, germanium bender, octave-up fuzz, and a chaotic five-knob starve box.
fuzz.long:
Four distinct fuzz circuits under one footswitch:

- Italian Hero — the big π-shaped New York sustain machine, in SIX era voicings (Delta, Ovis, Gotham, Cold War, Red Bear, Boutique) that trace the circuit's history from creamy violin sustain to scooped wall-of-doom, each tuned against pedal-direct captures
- I Know It — a component-accurate two-transistor germanium bender, all spitty mid-'60s British snarl
- Octavius — the upper-octave fuzz that made psychedelic solos ring like broken bells
- Fuzz Zachary — the gloriously unstable five-knob science experiment: bias starve, real compression bloom, and a Gate that takes it from tight and gated to self-oscillating squeal you can play

Everything is oversampled for clean, defined high-gain without the aliasing fizz that plagues naive digital fuzz. Works standalone or in the Hex Chain suite.

Free and open source (GPL-3). Names are original parodies and are not affiliated with any manufacturer.

nail.title: Hex Chain Nail
nail.short: Five-mode industrial distortion: fuzz, resonant filter, bitcrush, cab re-amp, ring-mod.
nail.long:
An industrial distortion block with five distinct topologies — each its own circuit, not one voicing knob: Broke (crude digital hard-clip with sample-rate decimation + bit-reduction), Dahnward (scooped high-gain preamp into a sweepable resonant band-pass), Delicate (a swollen, gherkin-fat fuzz with a wide filter sweep), Con Molars (a bright clip re-amped through a fixed miked-speaker voicing) and Yo, Hey Adrian! (a high-sustain clip into a switchable ring modulator). Controls: Mode, Drive, Filter, Texture, Level, plus a Ring Mod toggle for the Yo, Hey Adrian! mode. Oversampled; works standalone or in the Hex Chain suite.

Amp pairing: some modes and settings work into a clean amp or DI; the higher-gain settings generally want a driven amp — a cranked British master-volume half-stack is the classic move. Free and open source (GPL-3). Names are original and are not affiliated with any artist or manufacturer.

gate.title: Hex Chain Gate
gate.short: Low-CPU noise gate for high-gain rigs.
gate.long:
A clean, low-CPU noise gate with threshold and timing controls. Detection is decoupled from the fade, so it clamps hum and hiss promptly without chopping your sustain or truncating decay tails — in front of or after high-gain amps. Runs comfortably on every target including 32-bit Pi.

Free and open source (GPL-3).

comp.title: Hex Chain Compressor
comp.long:
A musical, low-CPU compressor for evening out picking dynamics and adding sustain — equally at home on guitar and bass, in front of a dirt pedal or across a clean signal. Runs on every target including 32-bit Pi.

Free and open source (GPL-3).

modfx.title: Hex Chain Modulation
modfx.short: Seven modulations in one block: two choruses, vibe, phaser, flanger, tremolo, rotary.
modfx.long:
A modulation block with SEVEN voicings: Lush-2 (warm bucket-brigade-style analog chorus), Uni-Verse (throbbing photocell swirl for your inner '69), Phaser, Flanger, Tremolo, Rotary (a spinning-speaker doppler swirl) and Nevermind Chorus (the watery, seasick analog chorus that defined a certain 1991 intro).

A Center Delay control (0–100 ms) shifts the delay line the chorus/flanger modulates around — from tight comb-filter shimmer to wide doubling. Unity-gain wet/dry mix, so engaging it never drops your level. Light on CPU; runs on every target including 32-bit Pi.

Free and open source (GPL-3). Names are original word play and are not affiliated with any manufacturer.

delay.title: Hex Chain Delay
delay.long:
Four delay machines in one block:

- Digital — clean, precise repeats
- Tape — warm saturation with wow & flutter that breathes like the real mechanism
- Echo Wreck — a multi-head drum echo with 12 head-combination patterns, from single slap to the full swirling all-heads wash
- Seraph — an angelic dual delay with rhythmic patterns (unison, dotted-8th, triplet and more), ducking that gets out of the way while you play, and lush modulation on the repeats

All modulated delay taps use smooth high-quality interpolation, so warble stays musical instead of gritty. Unity-gain mix — engaging it never drops your level.

Free and open source (GPL-3). Names are original word play and are not affiliated with any manufacturer.

reverb.title: Hex Chain Reverb
reverb.long:
A smooth plate reverb with size, tone and mix, a gently modulated tank for chorus-like density, and a unity-gain wet/dry blend so engaging it never drops your level — from a tight room to long, lush ambience. Heavier than the light effects but fine on Pi 4/5; usable on 32-bit Pi with headroom in mind.

Free and open source (GPL-3).

utility.title: Hex Chain Input Trim
utility.long:
A small but handy front-of-chain utility: clean gain trim, phase invert, a mains-hum filter (a comb of notches at 60 Hz and its harmonics), and a single-coil→humbucker voicing. The voicing re-voices a single-coil pickup toward one of three target bridge humbuckers — '59 Bucker (warm late-'50s vintage), Norse Hammer (hot ceramic) or Modern Flux (active hi-fi) — with an Amount control (0 = bypass). Minimal CPU; runs on every target.

Free and open source (GPL-3). Names are original parodies and are not affiliated with any manufacturer.

hexforge.title: Hex Forge
hexforge.short: Your entire guitar rig in one plugin — 11 amps, 7 drives, 4 fuzzes, mod/delay/reverb/wah/octave, cab mic + room, 50+ song-inspired presets, footswitch recall, and a full node-chain UI.
hexforge.long:
Hex Forge is the flagship — the whole Hex Chain signal chain in a SINGLE plugin, rebuilt around a modern node-chain interface: every block is a card you tap to edit, drag to reorder, and click to bypass, with per-model faceplates, live tone readouts and a built-in strobe tuner.

The blocks: input trim, noise gate, compressor, fuzz, drive, amp, cab, modulation, delay, reverb, wah, octave and the industrial 'Nail' stage — each independently bypassable and freely reorderable, so you build a complete board without patching a dozen plugins. And the depth inside each block is the point:

- AMP: ELEVEN original voicings (clean to modern high-gain), including the Cali V — a 9-mode three-channel switcher with a 5-band graphic EQ — and the Plexiglass with its jumpered Vol I + Vol II channels; every voicing rides a modeled power amp, with hum filtering and decay-aware noise conditioning on the hot channels.
- DRIVE: seven overdrive/boost/distortion voicings, from the green mid-hump legend to the mythical gold horse.
- FUZZ: four pedals — the multi-era Italian Hero, the germanium I Know It bender, the octave-ringing Octavius, and the self-oscillating Fuzz Zachary starve box.
- CAB: six loudness-matched built-in cabs (plus your own IRs), a DRAGGABLE mic-placement pad (cap→edge position, close→30 cm distance) and adjustable stereo room ambience — all preset-savable.
- Plus modulation (two choruses, vibe, phaser, flanger, tremolo, rotary with a 0–100 ms center-delay control), the four-machine delay (digital / tape / multi-head Echo Wreck / dual Seraph), plate reverb, wah, and an octaver with a microtonal quarter-tone shimmer voice.

A 32-bank / 128-slot preset engine ships loaded with 50+ song-inspired factory rigs — grunge, doom-pop ghouls, psychedelic prog, '60s guitar heroes, art rock, sludge metal, djent and more — every one researched against the original gear, level-matched so no preset jumps out, and recalled hands-free via A/B/C/D footswitches and hold-both bank chords. The factory pedalboard is pre-wired, so the pi-Stomp footswitches work the moment you load it — no MIDI setup. A dB-scaled master output with a transparent clip limiter keeps the whole rig stage-safe.

On 64-bit/desktop targets the amp and drive slots load your own .nam captures (the cab slot is pure IR/convolution); on 32-bit (patchbox-os-arm32) NAM is hidden and the algorithmic models are used. The heaviest plugin in the suite — best on Pi 4/5 and desktop. Free and open source (GPL-3). All device names are original parodies; no affiliation with any manufacturer or artist is implied.

wah.title: Hex Chain Wah
wah.long:
A wah with two modes: Auto, an envelope filter that sweeps with your picking dynamics, and Fixed, a parked "cocked-wah" midrange honk — so it works as a saved preset with no expression pedal needed. Resonance and range controls shape the vowel. Light on CPU; runs on every target including 32-bit Pi.

Works standalone or as part of the Hex Chain suite / Hex Forge. Free and open source (GPL-3).

octave.title: Hex Chain Octave
octave.short: Analog-style sub-octave + octave-up, plus a microtonal quarter-tone shimmer voice.
octave.long:
An analog-voiced octaver: a flip-flop sub-octave plus a rectifier octave-up, blended with dry via Up, Sub and Dry controls. Monophonic tracking — clean and singing on single notes, gnarlier on chords.

It also hides something no vintage octaver did: a pitch-tracked microtonal SHIMMER voice that shifts in quarter-tone (24-TET) intervals — quarter-steps up or down, neutral 2nds, 3rds and 6ths, or an octave-and-a-quarter — for shimmering, slightly-alien lead tones that sit between the notes on the fretboard. Light on CPU; runs on every target including 32-bit Pi.

Works standalone or as part of the Hex Chain suite / Hex Forge. Free and open source (GPL-3).
